key_insight: OCFormer learns a transformer-based mapping from simple, independent latent dynamics to coupled multi-agent trajectories, enabling fast planning across varying start and goal configurations.
engineering_relevance: The approach could accelerate collision-aware robot fleet planning by replacing repeated optimal-control solves with amortized inference.
method: Parameterize a latent-to-physical coordinate map with an agent-permutation-equivariant transformer.
Train without precomputed trajectories using Pontryagin Hamiltonian ODE residuals and boundary-matching loss.
Adapt to out-of-distribution conditions with lightweight L-BFGS fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 2D and 3D navigation experiments with up to 128 agents, approximately 220 ms inference for unseen boundary conditions, and adaptation in seconds.
watch_item: Physics-informed training alone does not establish hard collision-avoidance guarantees; safety and runtime require validation under deployment conditions.
paper_title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
